sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape/hardscape protection, mask glass adjacent to casings, mask light fixtures, set up access equipment. This spec owns casing-to-glass edge masking (RC-002). Siding masking is only required when application_method = spray.

tasks.name: Landscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along building perimeter where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent to trim work area. Brush: edge tarps at base. Spray: full width over plantings within drift zone.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of plantings within spray drift zone. Secure tarps against wind.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over walkways below trim work area. Canvas for crew traffic, plastic for overspray.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line. Extend coverage to drip/overspray zone. Canvas for crew traffic areas.

tasks.name: Window Glass Masking
tasks.description: Tape and paper/film mask all window glass adjacent to window casings being painted. This spec owns the casing-to-glass edge masking per RC-002. Apply exterior-grade UV-resistant tape (14-day rated minimum) at glass-to-casing edge, then apply masking paper or film over glass pane.

quality_notes.all: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed tight to casing edge — no paint bleed onto glass.

tasks.name: Door Glass Masking
tasks.description: Tape and paper/film mask all door glass adjacent to door casings being painted. Same masking technique as window glass.

quality_notes.all: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed tight to casing edge.

tasks.name: Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures mounted on or near trim. Bag and tape over fixture, or remove cover plate if accessible.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all fixtures on working elevation.

tasks.name: Siding Masking for Spray Application
tasks.description: Mask siding surfaces adjacent to trim when spraying. Tape and plastic along trim-to-siding edge. Required only when application_method = spray — brush application has minimal overspray and no siding masking needed.

quality_notes.all: Mask siding 12-18 inches from trim edge. Tape tight to trim-siding junction.

tasks.name: Brush Equipment & Access Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Stage brushes (angled sash 2.5 in + flat 3 in), paint pots, and materials. Brush is the PRIMARY method for exterior trim.

quality_notes.all: Verify access equipment stability. Stage materials within arm's reach of working position.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment & Access Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer with trim tips (211 for narrow, 313 for wider boards), 60-mesh filter, hoses. Stage materials.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size: 211 for casings/corners (3-4 in width), 313 for fascia/frieze/band (6-12 in width). 60-mesh black filter for latex.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape protection first -> Glass masking -> Fixture masking -> Siding masking (spray only) -> Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Substrate-driven prep: sand wood (80-120 grit) to remove mill glaze, scuff-sand PVC (220 grit), acetone wipe PVC cut edges, seal composite field-cut edges, spot-prime tannin knots on wood. Tasks activate based on substrate_material and substrate_state.

tasks.name: Sand Wood Trim — Remove Mill Glaze
tasks.description: Sand new wood trim with 80-120 grit to remove mill glaze and create adhesion profile. Hand blocks for edges and detail, orbital sander for flat runs. Mill glaze is the smooth, burnished surface created during manufacturing that prevents primer adhesion.

substrate_state_rules.notes: New wood trim has mill glaze. Sanding is mandatory for primer adhesion.
Already primed — no mill glaze removal needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Sand to remove glaze. Even scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand. Inspect for missed areas.
quality_notes.QT5: Full surface sand with systematic inspection. No glossy patches remaining.

tasks.name: Scuff Sand PVC Trim
tasks.description: Light scuff sand glossy PVC trim surfaces with 220-grit to create mechanical tooth for bonding primer adhesion. Do not sand aggressively — just break the gloss.

substrate_state_rules.notes: PVC in NC context is 'bare' — scuff sanding required for bonding primer adhesion on glossy surface.

quality_notes.QT3: Light scuff — break gloss on all surfaces.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform scuff. No glossy patches remaining.
quality_notes.QT5: Systematic scuff with inspection under raking light.

tasks.name: Acetone/Alcohol Wipe PVC Cut Edges
tasks.description: Wipe all cut edges of PVC trim with acetone or denatured alcohol. This seals open cells at cut edges and removes static charge that attracts dust. Required before bonding primer on PVC.

substrate_state_rules.notes: PVC in NC context. Acetone wipe for all cut edges.

quality_notes.all: Wipe every cut edge. Allow acetone to flash off before priming (1-2 minutes).

tasks.name: Edge-Seal Composite Trim Field Cuts
tasks.description: Brush-seal ALL field-cut edges on engineered wood composite trim (LP SmartSide TrimBoard) with primer + 100% acrylic latex paint. Unsealed cut edges absorb moisture into exposed wood fiber core, causing irreversible edge swelling. Non-negotiable WARRANTY REQUIREMENT.

substrate_state_rules.notes: All field-cut edges on composite must be sealed.
Assumed sealed during prior prime application.

quality_notes.all: EVERY cut edge sealed — butt joints, miters, field cuts. Non-negotiable for warranty.

tasks.name: Spot-Prime Tannin Knots (Wood Only)
tasks.description: Brush-apply alkyd or shellac-based stain-blocking primer to visible knots on tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir). Applied BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish coats.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Conditional on tannin-rich species. Required for cedar, redwood, fir.

quality_notes.QT4: All knots spot-primed. Inspect for bleed after drying.
quality_notes.QT5: All knots spot-primed. Double-coat large or resinous knots. Inspect for bleed after drying.

tasks.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust and debris from trim surfaces before primer application. Tack cloth for detailed areas, compressed air for complex profiles.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed from all trim surfaces. Surface ready for primer application.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Sand wood (80-120) OR scuff-sand PVC (220) OR edge-seal composite -> Acetone wipe PVC cut edges -> Spot-prime knots (wood, tannin species) -> Dust cleanup. Substrate_material determines which prep tasks activate.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Full Prime Coat
sop_modules.description: Full prime coat on all trim components. Three substrate-driven primer paths: (1) acrylic primer for wood/composite (SYS_EXT_TRIM_PRIMER_ACRYLIC), (2) bonding primer for PVC (SYS_EXT_TRIM_PRIMER_BONDING), (3) alkyd spot-prime for tannin knots is handled in prep module. Module SKIPPED entirely when substrate_state = SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by brush to all trim components. Angled sash brush for casings, corners, and sills; flat 3-inch brush for fascia, frieze, and band board. Primer product determined by substrate material (acrylic for wood/composite, bonding for PVC). Brush is the primary method for trim priming — penetrates grain and works into detail profiles.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Acrylic primer for wood and composite. Bonding primer (SYS_EXT_TRIM_PRIMER_BONDING) for PVC — primer selection driven by substrate_material dimension.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Work primer into grain. No holidays or thin spots.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform coverage. Consistent mil build. Inspect for missed areas.
quality_notes.QT5: Full coverage with systematic inspection. No holidays. Back-brush drips immediately.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by airless spray to long-run trim components (fascia, frieze, band board). Primer product determined by substrate material. Spray is secondary method for trim — used for long continuous runs where masking overhead is justified by production speed.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Acrylic for wood/composite, bonding for PVC — driven by substrate_material.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. No runs or sags.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. Inspect for coverage.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Method by application_method dimension. Substrate_material determines primer product (acrylic vs bonding). Module SKIPPED entirely when substrate_state = SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Joint Caulking
sop_modules.description: Caulk all trim joints AFTER primer coat (RC-003 correction). Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces than bare substrates. Covers trim-to-trim joints, corner joints, casing joints, trim-to-siding junctions. NEVER caulk: window weep holes, bottom overlap of siding boards, metal-to-wood flashing transitions. PVC: use solvent-based polymer or polyurethane — NEVER silicone.

tasks.name: Caulk Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply exterior paintable caulk to all trim-to-trim joints (corner joints, miters, butt joints, scarf joints) and trim-to-siding junctions. Tool smooth for clean appearance. Caulk rate: ~72 LF per tube (NC standard). PVC substrate: use polyurethane or solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) — NEVER silicone. Wood/composite: siliconized acrylic or polyurethane.

quality_notes.QT3: All joints caulked. Smooth tool. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead width. Precision tool smooth. Inspect for uniformity.
quality_notes.QT5: All joints caulked with precise, consistent bead. No voids, no overflow. Smooth to invisible joint line.

tasks.name: Caulk Window & Door Casing Joints
tasks.description: Caulk window casing perimeter joints (casing-to-wall/siding) and door casing perimeter joints. Tool smooth. Do NOT caulk window weep holes — these must drain freely. Casing-to-glass edge is taped/masked, not caulked.

quality_notes.QT3: All casing joints caulked. Clean bead.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect bead uniformity. No voids. Weep holes verified clear.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Module runs AFTER MOD_XTRM_PRIME (RC-003). Caulk trim joints first, then casing perimeter joints. Allow caulk to skin before finish coat. Polyurethane caulk on PVC joints requires 3-7 day cure before painting.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat on all trim components. Brush is the primary method (detail work). Spray for long continuous runs (fascia, frieze, band). Finish product by quality tier: QT3 = SYS_EXT_TRIM_FINISH_STANDARD, QT4/QT5 = SYS_EXT_TRIM_FINISH_PREMIUM. PVC with LRV < 55 = SYS_EXT_TRIM_FINISH_SOLAR (HARD STOP).

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by brush to all trim components. Angled sash brush for casings, corners, detail profiles, and sills. Flat 3-inch brush for fascia, frieze, and band board. Maintain wet edge. Brush is preferred for trim at all QT levels.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Clean edges. No drips or sags. Maintain wet edge.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform coverage. No brush marks visible at 6 ft. Clean, sharp edges at glass line.
quality_notes.QT5: Flawless brush work. No visible brush marks at 3 ft. Perfect edges.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray to long-run trim components. Tight fan patterns (211 for narrow, 313 for wide). Spray is secondary method — used for long fascia, frieze, and band runs where masking overhead is justified.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. No runs or sags. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect uniformity. Glass-smooth finish. No orange peel.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat. Spray tasks blocked in high wind — fall back to brush. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Interstage Inspection & Prep
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat, touch up defects. QT4: light sand between coats (150 grit). QT5: hand-sand between coats (220 grit) with raking light inspection. QT3: inspection and touch-up only, no intercoat sanding.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat on all trim for holidays, runs, sags, brush marks, and coverage defects. Mark defects for repair.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all visible defects.
quality_notes.QT5: Raking light inspection at 3 ft. Mark every defect. Inspect all profiles and edges.

tasks.name: Intercoat Sand Between Finish Coats
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats for mechanical adhesion and leveling. QT4: 150 grit light scuff. QT5: 220 grit hand-sand with raking light inspection. Not required at QT3.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand. Remove nibs and raised grain. Uniform scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT5: Hand-sand with 220 grit. Raking light inspection after sanding. No defects remaining.

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Repair defects found during interstage inspection. Brush touch-up of runs, holidays, and thin spots.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs.
quality_notes.QT5: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. No visible repair edges.

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust before second finish coat. Tack cloth on all trim surfaces.

quality_notes.all: All sanding dust removed from all trim surfaces before second finish coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> Sand (QT4/QT5 only) -> Touch up -> Dust removal -> Coat 2.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Runs once (1 interstage cycle).

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat on all trim components. Same application method as coat 1. Required at all tiers (QT3-QT5). Two finish coats standard for new construction exterior trim.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by brush. Same technique as coat 1. This is the appearance coat — highest standard of workmanship.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Clean edges. Final appearance coat.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform coverage. No brush marks at 6 ft. Perfect edges. Final coat.
quality_notes.QT5: Flawless final coat. No visible brush marks at 3 ft. Perfect edges, corners, and transitions.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray. Same method as coat 1. Final appearance coat.

quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final coat.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect uniformity. Glass-smooth finish. Final appearance coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. Required at all tiers (QT3-QT5). Two-coat finish is standard for NC exterior trim.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Final Inspection & Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of all trim components. Inspect for coverage, consistency, edge quality, caulk integrity. Touch up defects found.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished trim for coverage, consistency, edge quality at glass line, caulk integrity, and defects. Check elevated trim with binoculars at QT4+.

quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough. Scan for obvious defects.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for elevated trim. 6 ft viewing standard.
quality_notes.QT5: Comprehensive inspection. Binoculars for elevated. 3 ft standard on accessible trim. Raking light on primary elevations.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Blend repairs into surrounding finish.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects. Blend seamlessly at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT5: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft. Perfect final appearance.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations and all 8 trim component types -> Touch up -> Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Trim Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials (glass masking, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, siding masking), clean equipment, restore site.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, glass masking paper/film from windows and doors, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, siding masking (if spray). Check for tape residue on glass — remove immediately.

quality_notes.all: Remove all protection materials completely. Check glass for tape residue. Inspect landscape for overspray.

tasks.name: Clean Equipment
tasks.description: Clean brushes with appropriate solvent (water for latex, mineral spirits for alkyd spot primer). If spray: flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses.

quality_notes.all: Brushes cleaned and shaped. Sprayer flushed (if used). Tips and filters cleaned and stored.

tasks.name: Site Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, paint cans, acetone containers, used tack cloths. Leave site clean.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown -> Equipment cleaning -> Site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: Standard NC sequence: 1 prime + 2 finish coats. For bare substrate (SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD) at all QTs.
round_configurations.notes: Full sequence: prep -> prime -> caulk (prep phase) -> finish 1 -> interstage -> finish 2. Caulk module uses 'prep' phase but is sequenced between prime and finish per RC-003.

round_configurations.name: 2 Finish Coats Only (Field-Primed)
round_configurations.description: Skip prime, direct to 2 finish coats. For SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD only.
round_configurations.notes: Field prime already applied in prior mobilization. Caulk module still runs (prep phase). Prep module still runs for light surface prep.

key_differences_from_siding_specs: LF-based (not SF-based) — all 8 trim items measured in linear feet per PCA P10 one-foot rule
Multi-item spec (8 paintable items) vs single-item siding field
Brush is PRIMARY method (trim detail), spray is SECONDARY (long runs only) — opposite of siding where spray is primary
Caulk module is separate and sequenced AFTER prime (RC-003) — siding specs include caulk in prep module
Glass masking tasks (windows + doors) owned by this spec (RC-002) — siding specs do not mask glass
Siding masking required when spraying trim — not applicable to siding specs
Three substrate materials (wood/PVC/composite) with different prep paths — siding specs typically cover one substrate
QT3-QT5 range (no QT2) — trim is visible architectural detail requiring minimum QT3
Height modifiers more aggressive than general access modifiers (8ft=1.30 to 19ft=2.20) — trim requires fine brush detail at height

assumptions.value: Brush is the primary application method for exterior trim; spray is secondary for long continuous runs
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine: brush for precision/detail work, spray for production runs where masking is economical.

assumptions.value: Caulk module sequenced AFTER prime module — caulk adheres better to primed surfaces
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms caulk-after-prime sequence. This is a key difference from some siding specs that include caulk in the prep module before prime.

assumptions.value: This trim spec owns casing-to-glass edge masking (window and door glass protection)
assumptions.note: Window/door slab painting specs handle their own glass masking for sash/frame work. This spec handles casing-to-glass edge masking.

assumptions.value: QT2 excluded — exterior trim is minimum QT3
assumptions.note: Exterior trim is visible architectural detail. QT2 economy tier not applicable.

assumptions.value: Two finish coats required at all quality tiers (QT3-QT5) for NC exterior trim
assumptions.note: NC trim gets 2 finish coats at every tier. No single-coat option.

assumptions.value: Polyurethane caulk on PVC joints requires 3-7 day cure before painting
assumptions.note: Caulk scheduling impact: polyurethane requires extended cure. Siliconized acrylic can be painted after skinning.

assumptions.value: Trim-to-siding joint caulking may also be scoped under siding specs — engine must deduplicate
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for cross-spec caulk deduplication. Flagged for estimation engine project assembly logic.
